newsitem.title: USA: Kmart expects to post profit for Q1.
newsitem.headline: Kmart expects to post profit for Q1.

text.p: Kmart Corp, which last year posted a loss in the first quarter, said Monday it expects to report a profit for the same period this year.

Kmart's Chairman and Chief Executive Floyd Hall told investors during a meeting in New York that the discount store giant's same-store sales, or sales among stores open a year, were "slightly negative" for the month of April.
In a statement released by the company, Kmart said sales were weak because of a slowdown in business late last month and the shift in Easter sales to March from April this year.

Kmart's same-store sales for the first quarter were up 5.5 percent because business was strong during the first two months of the period, the retailer said. The company will report earnings for the first quarter, which ended April 30, on May 15.
Last year, Kmart's loss from continuing operations was $36 million, or $0.08 a share, during the first quarter. Its net loss was $99 million, or $0.21 a share.
Kmart also said it expects to modify terms of a $2.5 billion revolving bank credit facility to extend its maturity by one year to 2000. It expects to close the amendment to the facility on Tuesday.
Kmart operates 2,133 stores in the United States and 123 outlets abroad.
